# Titanfall 2 and Apex Legends maps: verified conversion knowledge

Recorded 11 October 2026 from the Apex-to-Titanfall conversion project. Latest
reviewed builds: Phase Runner 1.2.0 and Drop-Off 0.6.0, tested through Northstar.
This collection records observations from Apex rBSP 47 and Titanfall 2 rBSP 37.
It does not establish compatibility with every Apex season or engine build.

## Articles

- [BSP, model and serialized record layouts](binary-formats.md)
- [Collision decoding, ownership and traversable tunnels](collision.md)
- [Visibility, portals and measured engine limits](visibility-and-limits.md)
- [Materials, PBR, STBSP and texture residency](materials-and-streaming.md)
- [Lightmaps, character lighting and the multiplayer menu stage](lighting.md)
- [Entities, safety volumes, spawns and native game modes](entities-and-gameplay.md)
- [Phase Runner and Drop-Off conversion case studies](port-case-studies.md)
- [Native test harness and release validation](testing-and-packaging.md)
- [Design requirements for a future automatic converter](converter-design.md)

## Evidence policy

Measured binary capacities, serialized field ranges, project safety margins and
unverified ideas are different kinds of knowledge. Each article states its scope
and cites workspace-relative evidence paths. Those paths refer to the conversion
project; they are provenance references, not files hosted by Gravemind.

Structural validation is not proof of visual fidelity, successful loading is not
proof of collision, and a single-client run is not proof of multiplayer balance
or performance. Unknown formats and omitted objects must remain explicit.

The two ports bake selected static props into world meshes. Their world-index
budgets do not establish the limits of Titanfall's native model/entity renderer.
All-visible cells are a tested fallback, not a validated selective portal builder.

The articles contain technical findings and project-authored documentation.
Original game archives, extracted game assets and credentials are not included.

## Authoritative sources

`docs/conversion/APEX_TO_TITANFALL2.md`, the corresponding binary/layout/limit
ledgers, `docs/conversion/GAMEPLAY_MODES.md`, and the source scripts underpin
Phase Runner. Its static inventory retains explicitly versioned 1.0.0 provenance;
1.1.0 adds gameplay and 1.2.0 restores source safety areas.

For Drop-Off, prefer `docs/composite/validation.json`,
`docs/composite/local-repairs-2026-10-07.md`, and
`docs/composite/inventory-summary.json` for 0.6.0 measurements. Some introductory
paragraphs in `docs/composite/CONVERSION.md` retain older budgets, the old display
name and earlier feature descriptions. Its copied engine-limit ledger also has
a Phase Runner `current_release` section. Do not treat those as current Drop-Off
measurements. The current receipt resolves these discrepancies.

Future converter architecture in this collection is a proposal; it is not an
existing universal, one-command conversion tool.

# Titanfall 2 and Apex map binary formats

Scope: the tested Apex rBSP 47 inputs and Titanfall 2 rBSP 37 target. Serialized
little-endian layouts are not runtime engine structures. Dispatch on the file,
lump and game-lump versions before decoding; preserve unknown fields raw.

## BSP container and entity sources

The observed header is 2,064 bytes: `<4s3I` followed by 128 `<4I` lump descriptors.
Each descriptor holds offset, byte length, lump version and fourCC. Input maps can
have external `.bsp.XXXX.bsp_lump` payloads. Resolve external data before checking
stride and references, and record where each payload came from.

Changing the BSP version number is insufficient. Apex slots 0x12–0x16 carry
world BVH/packed-vertex/heightfield data without direct equivalents in the target
branch. Apex 0x2B/0x2C are not the target texture-string lumps. Matching record
sizes still require semantic and index validation.

Read the main entity lump and all available external entity partitions, including
environment, script, effects, sound and spawn files. Preserve original text,
duplicate keys, source IDs and partition provenance. Static props are principally
in `GAME_LUMP.sprp`, not just an `.ent` model list. Do not assume all placements
moved into an RPak. Geometry, placements and behavior are separate sources.

`GAME_LUMP` embedded payload addresses are absolute file offsets. Repacking the
outer BSP requires relocation of these addresses; copying the old directory
into a compacted container can leave invalid pointers. The project aligns output
lumps to 16 bytes, a writer choice distinct from an engine capacity.

## Observed serialized records

| Record | Size | Important fields or interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Lump descriptor | 16 | Four uint32 fields |
| Plane | 16 | Float XYZ normal plus distance |
| Apex BVH node | 64 | `<24h4I>`; axis-grouped bounds |
| Native lit-bump vertex | 44 | Position/normal references, albedo UV, color, lighting fields, packed tangent |
| Native mesh | 28 | Index start, uint16 triangle/local-vertex fields, material-sort reference, flags |
| Native material sort | 12 | Texture/lightmap/cubemap IDs, last local vertex, global vertex base |
| Mesh bounds / object-reference bounds | 32 | Native bounding data |
| Native cell node | 32 | Bounds, uint8 child/direct-reference counts, uint16 ranges |
| Collision grid cell | 4 | uint16 first-geoset/count |
| Collision geoset | 8 | Group/count and primitive-or-range word |
| Packed collision bounds | 16 | Signed16 center and extent triples plus flags |
| Collision brush | 32 | Center/extents, byte cut/bevel counts, ID and plane base |
| Triangle collision header | 44 | `<6h4i4f>` |
| Shadow mesh | 12 | Vertex base, triangle count, opacity/material-sort information |
| Character light probe | 48 | Coefficients, visibility, four light references, reserved data |
| Probe reference / parent | 20 / 28 | Spatial reference and KD access ranges |
| Tested `sprp` version-13 placement | 64 | `<7fH2B2H4f4b4B2H>` |
| STBSP material / column record | 24 / 24 | Name/GUID linkage; payload/coverage/bounds |

These sizes come from `docs/conversion/respawn_conversion_layouts.h` with static
assertions and `binary-layouts.json`. Drop-Off reports game-lump version 50;
do not reinterpret it blindly using Phase Runner's version-13 placement schema.
Retain the appropriate parser and source map's version metadata.

## Compiled model recovery

RMDL/VG/PHY can exist even when QC/SMD exports are absent. The tested VG header
is 160 bytes, magic `0x47567430`, version 1, with eighteen uint64 offset/count
values starting at byte 16. Mesh records are 72 bytes (`<18I`), LOD records eight
bytes (`<2hf`). Vertex flags and stride determine float versus packed positions.
Skinned flags `0x5000` require skeleton processing outside this static decoder.

Retain RMDL skin and submesh material assignments. Resolve OBJ negative indices
against each array length at the face being read, not the completed file.
The extraction pipeline's UV inversion and triangle order `[0,2,1]` must be
applied once, followed by winding, normal and tangent-handedness checks.

For the tested sources, XYZ axes are unchanged. Phase Runner is translated by
subtracting `[26000,19000,0]`; Drop-Off does not use that recentering. Apply a
map's transform once to geometry, collision, lights, bounds, probes and entities.
The project maps parser angle components to native pitch/yaw/roll in the tested
ordering; do not infer an XYZ swap from parser field names or culling symptoms.

## Sources

`docs/conversion/binary-layouts.json`, `docs/composite/binary-layouts.json`,
`docs/conversion/respawn_conversion_layouts.h`, `read_vg_static.py`,
`stage_prop_geometry.py`, `compact_preview_bsp.py`, and both conversion guides.
Use these versioned definitions rather than treating the table as universal.

# Apex-to-Titanfall collision decoding and ownership

Scope: tested source world BVH, inline STAR and IRPS/embedded-model collision;
target native brush/triangle grid. Heightfields and complete contents equivalence
are not implemented as general conversion backends.

## Decode the source collision frame correctly

An Apex BVH node is `<24h4I>` (64 bytes). Bounds are grouped by axis: four minima
then four maxima for each axis. They are not four interleaved XYZ child boxes.
Child references are derived from words shifted right eight bits; contents and
type bits also occupy those words. Retain source model ranges, packed vertex
scale/offset, and `first_vertex`. The tested world uses `first_vertex=1`; omitting
it caused collision to drift from the visible surfaces.

Observed node kinds: 0 node, 1 empty, 3 compound, 4 regular triangle, 5 packed
triangle, 6 regular quad, 7 packed quad, 8 inline STAR and 9 static-prop reference.
Compound and inline blocks require their own palettes, alignment and frame.
Signed global coordinates and unsigned inline-local coordinates are different
decoders; do not merge them by convenience.

The tested PHY has a 20-byte `<5I>` header and relative-pointer IRPS graph. Root
descriptors contain four int64 relative pointers; group records are 144 bytes,
convex pieces 64. Vertices are float XYZ; face lists use signed-byte indices
terminated by -1. Validate pointers relative to their owning base, bounds and
winding, then triangulate polygon faces. Some tested RMDLs provide an embedded
BVH pointer at offset 532; this is a version-specific fallback.

## Native collision representation

| Lump | Role |
| --- | --- |
| 0x55 / 0x56 | Grid and uint16 first/count cells |
| 0x57 / 0x58 | Geosets and packed bounds |
| 0x59 / 0x5A | Primitive words and bounds |
| 0x5B | Contents palette |
| 0x5C–0x5F | Brushes, plane offsets, side properties and texture vectors |
| 0x42 / 0x44 / 0x45 | Triangle words, packed nodes and 44-byte headers |
| 0x60 / 0x61 | Bevel starts and shared bevel indices |

Primitive words encode kind in the top byte, target index in bits 8–23 and
contents index in the low byte. Kind 0 is brush; `0x40` is triangle header.
Multi-primitive geosets reference a range rather than one primitive. Brushes
have six implicit axial planes plus explicit cuts/bevels; side properties matter.

Triangle headers use `<6h4i4f>` for flags, texture metadata, counts, starts,
origin and scale. Triangle words use a 10-bit base, two seven-bit deltas and
orientation bits. The 96-triangle grouping is a project choice; the helper
supports up to 300. Centers and extents must each fit signed16. Clipping vertex
coordinates to ±32760 does not guarantee representable bounding extents.

## Solidity and ownership

Use brushes for closed convex solids. Concave rocks, tunnels, ring frames and
rails need triangle surfaces or deliberate compound decomposition. A whole-prop
AABB can fill a tunnel and create invisible barriers. Foliage cards should not
become solid automatically. Retain source collision independent of render LOD.

A static prop can already own collision in the source world BVH even if its
separate PHY is missing or its visual is omitted. Check decoded owner IDs and
world bounds before adding another collider. Drop-Off containers 5287 and 5288
were invisible while their higher-detail world collision worked. Restoring their
LOD3 visuals required no collider changes; the visual top differs slightly from
the higher-fidelity collision, a documented LOD approximation.

Distinguish stored from active collision. Phase Runner's baseline stores 7,654
brushes and 25,948 triangle headers, but its active grid contains 7,134 brushes
and 25,866 headers. Disabled caps can remain serialized without being active.
Apply the current tunnel/catwalk/tree overlays to historical ownership ledgers.

## Tunnel barriers and intentional clips

Remove only identified caps intersecting a verified passage. Toolclip/nodraw
surfaces can intentionally close inaccessible rooms or roofs. In Drop-Off, north
and diagonal clips initially removed as obsolete barriers were restored after
comparison with source layout and user confirmation. A visually empty space is
not enough evidence to delete its collider.

Phase Runner needed visible ring-frame collision where an original portal PHY
represented a filled disk. Its adapted catwalk has an 80-unit deck, 71-unit
passage clearance and 42-unit rails with open entries. Native movement-hull
checks cover the route; a downward line trace alone does not prove traversability.

## Sources

`decode_collision.py`, `read_prop_physics.py`, `native_triangle_collision.py`,
`rebuild_complete_collision.py`, `repair_tunnel_passages.py`,
`docs/conversion/tunnel-collision-repair.json`, `docs/conversion/catwalks.json`,
`docs/conversion/collision-ownership-baseline.json`,
`docs/dropoff-source-layout-2026-10-07.md`, and Drop-Off's 0.6.0 repair receipt.

# Titanfall map visibility, portals and measured limits

Scope: world-baked render path in the tested installed Titanfall 2 engine.
These are not universal map dimensions or a native-model total-prop limit.

## Why converted objects disappeared

The project reproduced position- and angle-dependent disappearance of pipes,
stairs, rocks and props. Failures involved native index submission capacity,
material/opaque/alpha partitions, access-path bounds and camera-cell data.
Looking straight ahead versus up/down does not prove different XYZ axes or
an out-of-bounds gameplay rule. The tested sources use unchanged XYZ axes.

Conservative native all-visible cell/access-path structures removed these
failures. Keep actual mesh bounds geometric; widen camera access envelopes rather
than falsifying geometry bounds. Phase Runner's tested camera envelope spans
`[-16384,-16384,-8192]` to `[16384,16384,8192]`. This is a project visibility
envelope, not the maximum playable map dimensions.

Changing mesh order or partitions requires remapping all cell/object references,
including transparent meshes. Changing lightmap pages can split meshes and
therefore changes padding, draw keys and visibility references too.

Earlier selective portal graphs culled the sky and interiors, producing
hall-of-mirrors artifacts. A future selective implementation needs watertight
cells, oriented apertures, connected interior/exterior paths, sky propagation,
state-dependent doors, and camera sweeps inside and outside each passage.
It remains unvalidated; conservative visibility plus optimization is the tested
fallback, with a larger simultaneous render cost.

## Capacities versus policies

| Constraint | Value | Evidence class |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Submitted world indices | 3,145,728 | Audited native capacity, engine RVA 0xB72AF |
| World draw batches | 2,048 | Audited native capacity, engine RVA 0xB7304 |
| Material sorts | 8,192 | Native loader bitset capacity |
| Mesh reference/local vertex/primitive index | 65,535 maximum index | uint16 serialized range |
| Brush cut/bevel and cell child/direct-reference count | 255 | uint8 serialized range |
| Packed center and extent | signed16, maximum 32,767 | Serialized range; check both independently |
| Phase Runner world index margin | ≤95% | Project safety policy |
| Drop-Off recovery margin | ≤90% | Project safety policy |
| Phase Runner static batches | <512 | Project safety policy; light masks can multiply batches |
| Local vertex ceiling / collision group size | 60,000 / 96 triangles | Conservative writer choices |

Native mesh index cost is `3 * (triangles + (triangles & 1))`: odd triangle
counts receive pair padding. Budget the padded sum per mesh, not three times
the scene's active triangles. Disabled degenerate slots still occupy submission
storage. Dynamic light masks can split the base static draw keys at runtime.

Observed engine SHA-256:
`58eb1a1b44b30275bdd21368de264d856bc310d37d93a0f76f111f0026913487`.
Observed client SHA-256:
`002b36487fec7c98882929fbccdb506d0146bbf3270cbb964a4d21c5edf7eebc`.
RVAs and capacities must be re-audited against changed binaries.

## Reviewed budgets

| Snapshot | World indices | Meshes | Static batches | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Phase Runner documented geometry baseline | 2,924,184 | 4,982 | 479 | 92.96% of observed capacity; later entity/safety repairs preserve geometry |
| Drop-Off 0.6.0 | 2,830,530 | 3,024 | 353 | 89.980%; about 200 more triangles under its 90% policy, depending on padding |

Drop-Off has 942,146 serialized triangle slots, of which 942,014 are active.
Its 132 disabled slots are 108 start covers and 24 orphan-lamp faces. Capacity
checks establish that the audited submission fits, not a stable frame rate or
unlimited dynamic effects. Further substantial recovery needs geometry savings
or a separately validated model/visibility backend.

No universal map-size limit, native entity/prop total, VRAM cap, selective portal
capacity or support for all Apex versions was established.

## Sources

`audit_world_draw_budget.py`, `guard_native_sort_capacity.py`,
`repair_camera_visibility.py`, `native_preview_cells.py`,
`docs/conversion/engine-limits.json`, and
`docs/composite/local-repairs-2026-10-07.md` / `validation.json`.
The copied Composite engine-limit ledger's `current_release` is Phase Runner;
use the 0.6.0 receipt for current Drop-Off usage.

# Titanfall native materials, PBR and STBSP

Scope: the project's native world-material adaptation. The tested target uses
RPak version 7 and `matl` version 12. Apex shaders are not directly transplantable.

## Materials and correct texture assignment

Read RMDL skin and submesh material slots and keep original albedo UVs. Losing
the submesh mapping made control-room consoles display unrelated atlas fragments.
Do not guess transparency from a material slot number: painted Hammond cargo
containers must remain opaque; actual opacity/decal masks select alpha passes.

The native adaptation recovers albedo, normal, gloss and specular channels.
Metalness/roughness needs an intentional BRDF conversion; renaming source channels
does not reproduce source shading. Source vertex colors, layered blends, wind,
animated screens and full reflection behavior remain incomplete.

Native world materials require compatible shader dependencies, uberbuffer,
glue, rasterizer, depth and blend states, and matching depth passes. Lowering
texture alpha on an opaque material does not make correct transparent glass.
Dedicated compatible alpha/transparent passes and TEXDATA flags must agree.

## Dependency closure and loading failures

Check every texture, shader and pass dependency against the package and required
native common/Coliseum packs. One decal shader referenced an unmounted Glitch
asset and stalled loading. The fixed conversion embeds compatible dependencies
with distinct GUIDs. Validate a cold launch and stock-map reload; having visited
a dependency map earlier must not be required.

GUID existence checks alone are insufficient. In Drop-Off, inheriting a glass
template's unrelated texture table stalled startup despite available GUIDs.
Alpha materials must bind only their intended recovered channels. Broad map-regex
pak loading and raw dependency preloading also caused lifecycle/hang failures
in earlier experiments; retain the actually tested pack order and reload tests.

Use neutral fallback materials for missing assets rather than an unrelated atlas.
Report source aliases, rendered face counts, shader provenance and unresolved
dependencies separately. `_wldc` aliases and derived layer alpha are important
for the recovered ground/dirt overlays.

## STBSP versus STARPak

Titanfall requires a matching STBSP material catalogue alongside these BSPs.
The tested STBSP version is 8.0, header 392 bytes, magic `0xCB00CBB5`. Six uint64
offset/count descriptors begin at byte 168. Material-info and spatial-column
counts are record counts with 24-byte strides; other blocks use byte counts.
Observed physical block order is `[1,2,3,0,4,5]`, with absolute file offsets.

Material records link string names to 64-bit asset GUIDs. Columns carry
payload-relative offset, size, coverage and packed XY bounds. The ports use
resident textures and empty coverage columns. This fulfils the tested catalogue
requirements; it does not implement full spatial mip streaming. STBSP and texture
STARPak have distinct roles and must not be conflated.

Drop-Off 0.6.0 has 231 native catalogue materials and resident textures capped at
1024 pixels. That cap is a project quality/residency choice, not a native engine
limit. A future streaming backend needs verified coverage/residency semantics,
preserved referenced STARPak offsets, and movement tests under actual VRAM pressure.
Stage referenced stream extents into owned sparse copies; never truncate inputs.

## Foliage and depth separation

Phase Runner's twenty firs use fixed author LOD2: 62 bark plus 952 foliage
triangles per tree. Leaf alpha combines albedo alpha and opacity with coverage-
preserving mip generation. Compatible two-sided foliage is retained. Leaf cards
are excluded from static casting to avoid rectangular shadows; trunks cast.
No wind animation or dynamic LOD is recovered by world baking.

Z-fighting fixes separate only render layers and preserve collision bytes.
Phase Runner used 0.08-unit layer offsets (0.16 for stripes); Drop-Off's selected
ground overlay used 0.24. These are measured local repairs, not universal texture
offsets. Record applied edits and hashes so rebuilding cannot apply them twice.

## Sources

`prepare_composite_materials.py`, `build_preview_stbsp.py`,
`stage_rpak_streams.py`, `docs/conversion/loading-repair.json`,
`docs/arena-repairs-2026-10-06.md`, `docs/composite/missing-materials.json`,
and both conversion guides. See [lighting](lighting.md) for shading diagnosis.

# Titanfall lightmaps, character probes and menu-stage isolation

Scope: project ray-baked sun/sky/local lighting, not a production GI or reflection
bake. PBR material recovery and baked illumination are separate tasks.

## Native lightmap and probe relationships

Observed SKY A uses RGBM in linear units:
`decoded_rgb = rgb * (alpha * 3.984375 + 0.015625)`.
SKY B direction decodes as `rgb * 2.007874 - 1`.
RTL A packs four six-bit local-light entries plus an eight-bit page; unused
entry is 63. RTL B carries visibility channels and a half-resolution plane.
The light-page table must match native hardware light indexing.

World-light records are 112 bytes in the tested lump version. Ambient entries
are filtered out of the hardware light table, so a WORLD_LIGHTS index is not a
hardware index. In the tested configuration, sun world slot 1 maps to hardware
slot 0. Character dynamic-light references also apply native reserved offsets.

Character probes are 48 bytes with fixed-point ambient coefficients (divide by
8192), visibility bytes and four light references. Rebuild their KD/access
structure and remap references against the filtered hardware table. Phase Runner
has 39,819 gameplay plus two menu probes, with 16,383 KD nodes. Drop-Off has
2,907 probes. These are map measurements, not format capacity limits.

## Physical multiplayer menu area

Titanfall multiplayer maps contain a physical pilot/Titan customization stage.
Mixing its environment/light slots with gameplay produced menu-character shadows
and a small rectangular lit region around the camera. Incorrect probe mapping
also left the player without expected native lighting.

Retain a separate menu environment and stage probes. Phase Runner isolates its
stage near `[-11776,11856,12736]`; this is a conversion choice. Drop-Off's 0.5.0
repair relocates all menu anchors and lighting together outside the photographic
sky sphere. Moving only the camera or one mesh is insufficient. Verify pause
menu transitions and views from the gameplay area.

Keep photographic sky geometry out of opaque caster/occlusion masks. The
converted skies are sphere-projection approximations, not exact source skyboxes.

## Triangle-shaped wall shadows

Drop-Off's wall marks disappeared with native fullbright, supporting a lighting
diagnosis rather than an albedo fault. Sparse 4x4 charts sampled tiny trim shadows
at triangle vertices and spread them over large white panels. Global nearest-
sample padding could also copy another chart's values into a gutter.

0.6.0 first confined every old chart's padding to its own six valid samples,
preserving those samples byte-for-byte. Padding repair alone did not remove the
wall marks. It then rebaked 1,302 large painted-wall triangles with 32x32 charts
(351 raster samples) and 948 smaller triangles with 16x16 (105 samples), using
slightly inset receivers and local gutters. Scope is the vertical painted-metal
panels near both control entrances, not the entire map.

New charts occupy spare space on atlas page 3, starting at rows 1248 and 1920.
No atlas page or texture-memory increase was needed. Reserve these rectangles
before subsequent appends and reject overlaps.

The native atlas page is bound by material sort per mesh. Updating vertex UVs
alone initially bound the wrong page. Split affected meshes by page, repartition
their indices with odd-triangle pair padding, and remap bounds/visibility. Tests
preserve old active faces and all non-lightmap vertex attributes. Reviewed native
captures greatly reduce the severe zigzags; this is not proof that every sparse
chart artifact elsewhere is fixed.

## Baker scope and verification

Phase Runner uses seven lightmap pages and thirty interior lights. Drop-Off uses
four 2048-pixel pages and sixty selected local lights; source spots are approximated
as point lights. Neither has bounced GI or freshly baked reflection cubemaps.

Verify charts, page bindings, RTL IDs and probe references structurally, then
inspect native horizontal/up/down, interior and player views. Preserve logs and
camera metadata; a successful bake calculation does not establish native output.

## Sources

`docs/conversion/character-lighting.json`, `interior-lights.json`,
`apply_baked_lighting.py`, retained C++ baker sources,
`docs/composite/screens-and-menu-2026-10-07.md`,
`docs/composite/local-repairs-2026-10-07.md`, `repair_composite_local.py`,
`test_composite_local.py`, and `docs/composite/validation.json`.

# Map entities, safety volumes and Northstar gameplay adaptation

Read source BSP and external `.ent` partitions, but distinguish source geometry
from behavior. A matching classname or imported brush does not establish that
Apex scripts, conditional states, doors, audio or effects work in Titanfall.

## Conditional geometry and source-linked ropes

Drop-Off had nine `func_brush_arenas_start_zone` models, six around active spawns
and three in a remote alternate area. Treating their start covers as permanent
world geometry covered the doors. Exactly 108 active-cover render/shadow faces
are disabled. Native traces across all six active exits were already clear, so
nearby collision was not removed speculatively.

Source `zipline` and `zipline_end` GUID links define two real rope pairs. Preserve
their endpoints and adapt them to native `move_rope` / `keyframe_rope`; sag is
approximate. Earlier guessed upper-platform routes were removed in 0.3.0.
Drop-Off 0.6.0 retains only these source routes:

| Route | Start XYZ | End XYZ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| West | -390.012, 4178.35, 283.789 | -754.951, 2764.85, 341.27 |
| East | 393.988, 4174.35, 283.789 | 758.429, 2764.76, 341.27 |

Invisible room/roof clips can be intentional even without visible doors. Restore
closure visuals or adapt behavior deliberately; do not infer an opening from an
empty viewport. Drop-Off's eight scripted Apex doors are not implemented.

## Native safety triggers

Source `*coll0`, `*coll1`, ... blobs are decoded in numeric order. The tested
descriptor is 56 bytes with leaf start at offset 28. Leaf header is `<4B4f>`
(vertex/face/triangle/quad counts, XYZ frame and scale). Positions are signed
int16, scaled by `65535 * leaf_scale`, then translated by the frame origin.
Unsigned decoding wrongly displaced fall volumes and could place a kill plane
above the arena. This is not the same coordinate rule as every world BVH leaf.

Rebuild each convex native trigger with local plane keys
`*trigger_brush_B_plane_P` and `*trigger_bounds_mins/maxs`, preserving intended
class, damage and boundary settings. Remove obsolete source collision blobs/model
references and apply the map transform once. Target entities live in the main
lump with empty external-partition tag in these builds.

Phase Runner 1.2.0 converts 82 source out-of-bounds entities and one fall hurt
volume; one wholly remote boundary is omitted. Countdown activation/reset was
verified in the native client. Drop-Off retains 21 source out-of-bounds and five
hurt volumes. The project clips convex pieces to its target coordinate domain;
that is a conversion policy rather than universal native bounds.

## Teams, spawns and objectives

Phase Runner uses IMC team 2 west and Militia team 3 east, preserving existing
assignments/spectators and assigning fallback players to the smaller team.
1.1.0 adds 92 entities: 24 pilot starts, 42 neutral pilot respawns, 12 outdoor
Titan respawns, six Titan starts, two flags, three hardpoints and three captures.
Native respawn ratings retain frontline, enemy sightline and cooldown logic.

CTF uses `info_spawnpoint_flag` with explicit team numbers. Hardpoint uses
`info_hardpoint` linked by `triggerTarget` to `trigger_capture_point`; six local
axial planes define each 640x640x224 capture box. Trigger volumes are not solid
walls. Fastball uses the native Northstar Buddy/panel hooks with alternating
origin/angle vectors; it needs more than ordinary human spawn markers.

| Identifier | Phase Runner adaptation |
| --- | --- |
| `aitdm` | Attrition spawns present; AI navigation still missing |
| `tdm`, `ps`, `ffa` | Native spawn pools/team starts; neutral FFA points |
| `ctf` | Two flag bases and native pickup/return/scoring setup |
| `cp` | Three capture/amp objectives |
| `fastball` | Buddy throw locations and three native panels |
| `lts`, `ttdm`, `mfd` | Titan/team or shared native spawn setup as appropriate |

Observed pilot markers were floor/hull checked; Titan clearance uses a
200x200x400 hull. Single-client objective activation is not proof of complete
multiplayer matches, balance, all trajectories or all mode lifecycle behavior.
An AIN revision and nonempty navigation graph are needed for native Attrition
AI waves. Adding spawn entities cannot supply grunt paths or deployment routes.

Drop-Off targets Skirmish, Pilots vs Pilots and FFA, with 24 team human starts,
24 neutral human respawns, six team Titan starts and six neutral Titan respawns.
It has no CTF/Hardpoint/Fastball setup or AI navigation. Dropship intro/evac are
disabled in both normal map adaptations; Phase Runner Fastball retains its
native throw intro. Do not claim dropship or evac support from team spawns alone.

`build_phase_runner_modes.py`, `decode_source_trigger_volumes.py`,
`docs/arena-repairs-2026-10-06.md`,
`docs/dropoff-source-layout-2026-10-07.md`, and current Drop-Off omission ledger.

# Phase Runner and Drop-Off: verified conversion case studies

Reviewed 11 October 2026; latest tested project releases were built 6–7 October.
These are playable visual/collision adaptations, not full Apex gameplay ports.

| Map | Apex source | Titanfall command | Northstar package | Reviewed release |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Phase Runner | `mp_rr_arena_phase_runner` | `map mp_phase_runner` | `PhaseRunner` | 1.2.0 |
| Drop-Off | `mp_rr_arena_composite` | `map mp_arena_composite` | `ArenaComposite` | 0.6.0 |

Both tested source BSPs are version 47; targets are version 37. Drop-Off is the
displayed map name, while Composite remains the internal source/package name.
Map labels/loading art are adapted separately from physical map data.

## Phase Runner

Source coordinates are recentered by subtracting `[26000,19000,0]`. The release
uses conservative all-visible geometry, world-baked static props, source collision
plus targeted tunnel repairs, native character lighting, and interior illumination.
An authored catwalk/rail adaptation improves tunnel traversal.

Twenty firs are complete fixed LOD2 rather than player-sized brush impostors.
The grounding audit found one trunk about 47.6 units above rendered snow. Nearby
omitted props were small vegetation, not a structural support. Nine trunks were
lowered eight units below minimum sampled support; eleven embedded trunks stayed
unchanged. The correction propagates to visual, collision and lighting transforms.
Grounding is a deliberate local repair, not a rule to snap all source objects.

The static inventory is a 1.0.0 snapshot: 5,425 included of 16,376 placements
inside the arena, 10,951 omitted across 68 model types, and 486 outside the filter.
Foliage (9,537 omitted) dominates, followed by rocks (527) and industrial props
(339). Do not add the twenty firs again to these documented included counts;
later 1.1.0 gameplay and 1.2.0 safety changes do not represent new recovered props.
Compiled model availability and target inclusion remain separate properties.

The documented geometry baseline has 972,628 triangles, 2,924,184 padded indices,
4,982 meshes and 479 static batches. Seven lightmap pages, thirty local interior
lights and 39,821 character probes are recorded. AI navigation, full shader/FX
parity, dynamic source behavior and full spatial mip streaming remain incomplete.

## Drop-Off

0.6.0 accounts for all 8,356 source static placements:

| Disposition | Placements |
| --- | ---: |
| Included | 4,264 |
| Excluded by all-visible draw budget | 2,051 |
| Remote/menu/backdrop selection exclusion | 1,884 |
| Source asset not recovered | 147 |
| Removed detached wind shield | 1 |
| Removed orphan attached lamp | 1 |
| No rendered sections after atmosphere/glow filters | 8 |

The local-origin filter has 6,472 placements and is a project selection policy.
Budget exclusions can be recoverable assets, not missing files. Fourteen selected
solid placements have no decoded source collision (small cable stoppers, puddle
decals and bamboo). Neutral fallback source signage covers 564 rendered triangles;
`empty_model` covers one. Source layered shaders, animation, reflections, spot
light fidelity, doors, audio and particle behavior are incomplete.

0.6.0 restores source server supports 2914/2916 and stacked tank containers
5287/5288 at original transforms using complete LOD3, adding 910 triangles.
The containers' existing world collision is retained. Lamp 5093 belonged to the
previously removed wind shield 4924; its 24 draw/shadow faces are disabled.
No new guessed collider fills that gap.

The wall-lighting repair targets 2,250 painted-wall triangles with higher-resolution
charts and proper native page bindings. Final cost: 942,146 serialized slots,
942,014 active triangles, 2,830,530 padded indices, 3,024 meshes and 353 batches.
The 90% project policy is nearly reached; substantial new props require savings.

35 regressions passed. Native captures cover all four reported locations and
both control entrances. Three native contact rays hit retained colliders.
Postmatch returned to the lobby, then stock Coliseum and Drop-Off reloaded in
the same process without logged script errors. This does not identify the cause
of an earlier user crash or establish multiplayer stability/performance.

## Version provenance

Use current receipts rather than historical summaries. Drop-Off's initial guide
still contains its old name and an earlier 86% budget. The copied engine-limit
JSON's current-release measurements describe Phase Runner, not Drop-Off. The
0.3.0 source-layout record supersedes 0.2.0 guessed rope placements/removed clips.
0.6.0 validation and repair records are authoritative for its final native build.

## Sources

`docs/conversion/trees.json`, `docs/conversion/tree-grounding-before.json`,
`docs/composite/inventory-summary.json`, `docs/composite/MISSING_CONTENT.md`,
`docs/composite/validation.json`, and versioned repair documents.

# Native Northstar map testing and clean releases

The project has an opt-in Squirrel/Python harness for launch, map load, camera
positioning, collision queries, screenshots and lifecycle checks. It is a testing
mod, not part of the released map and not a DLL plugin.

## Harness architecture

The controller listens on loopback `127.0.0.1:39131`; UI, client and server script
contexts poll it independently through Northstar HTTP with `-allowlocalhttp`.
Per-session bearer authentication protects the local queue. Commands are delivered
and acknowledged by the appropriate context; expired queued commands are cancelled.
No harness credentials or raw session files belong in knowledge-base entries.

A separate `R2MapHarness` profile stages current packages, core Northstar mods
and the harness. Normal `R2Northstar` remains separate. Replace owned staging
directories rather than merging: stale BSPs previously shadowed the new package.
Only stop the game process owned by the controller.

Readiness needs fresh UI/client/server heartbeats at the requested level and a
new generation ID after load. `load` does not restage modified runtime bytes;
stop/relaunch after a package change. A successful command can otherwise act on
a lobby reached after match end, so capture and trace metadata must verify map.

## Repeatable checks

Camera origins are eye positions, player origins are feet, and angles are native
pitch/yaw/roll degrees. Camera mode hides HUD/weapon. Freezing input does not stop
gravity; it is not a guarantee the player remains at the requested coordinates.

Routes record map, mode, labeled eye origins, angles, FOV and settling time. Native
screenshots are awaited as new files, dimension-checked and converted to previews.
Adjacent metadata includes active map, camera, time and SHA-256. Do not substitute
an unrelated desktop image when capture fails. Visual review remains necessary.

Useful sequences include cold launch, both team starts, ground/up/down views,
interior camera sweeps, selected line traces, full pilot/Titan hull probes,
menu-stage transitions, forced postmatch, stock-map load and converted-map reload.
Line contacts do not prove a full route is traversable. Start-solid and missing
ground support must be explicit failures. Export logs with credentials redacted.

The owned launch also depends on a working EA/Origin session. A verified
“Lost connection to Origin” error blocked one screenshot run; reconnecting EA
allowed the final reload checks to complete. Distinguish authentication/environment
failures from malformed maps instead of repeatedly changing geometry.

Switching out of a Titan-only mode previously triggered a stock Titan-selection
UI assertion. The harness uses a fresh process for such transitions and retains
the failed run as evidence; it does not patch stock gameplay/UI to hide it.

## Structural checks before launch

Validate finite coordinates, version/stride, all references/ranges, absolute
game-lump relocation, material dependencies and slots, opaque/alpha partitions,
reachable mesh references, native index padding, collision contents/ownership/grid,
signed bounding extents, chart overlap/page binding, light/probe mappings, safety
triggers and spawn marker links. Keep old byte/face comparisons for targeted
repairs where full rebuilding is unnecessary.

## Packaging and rollback

A clean player ZIP contains the runtime Northstar directory (`mod.json`, `mod/`,
`paks/`), short install README and optional actual game screenshot. Development
scripts, input archives, ledgers, test logs and credentials remain outside it.
Server and clients need matching versions; disable old copies and restart.

Hash every source runtime file and verify archive membership and extracted bytes.
Stage and hash installation before replacing the owned mod; retain the previous
version for rollback. Separate map packages must not overwrite each other.
Snapshot edits atomically; hardlinked backups require detach-before-write or an
in-place write can silently alter the backup.

Drop-Off 0.6.0's clean ZIP has 22 members: twenty runtime files, README and native
screenshot. Its installed 0.5.0 was retained. Final single-client validation is
documented separately from binary checks; multiplayer performance and balance
remain unestablished.

## Sources

`test-harness/README.md`, `test-harness/harness.py`, `test-harness/test_harness.py`,
`Run-MapHarness.ps1`, `verify_composite_local_runtime.py`,
`package_player_mods.py`, `install_arena_repair_releases.py`, and map validation
receipts. The HTTP API reference used by the harness is
https://docs.northstar.tf/Modding/reference/northstar/httprequests/.

# Requirements for a future Apex-to-Titanfall map converter

Status: proposed architecture informed by tested ports. The current implementation
is a set of project scripts with retained intermediate/template dependencies,
not an arbitrary-map, clean one-command converter. Supported evidence is limited
to the tested source BSP 47 and target BSP 37 combinations.

## Stages

1. Inspect immutable hashed BSP/VPK/RPak/STARPak/PHY inputs, versions, external
   lumps, entities, static placements and dependencies.
2. Extract only referenced assets into owned caches, preserving stream offsets
   and source hashes; leave original archives read-only.
3. Normalize geometry, transforms, material slots, collision and ownership into
   a typed intermediate representation; version-dispatch unknown layouts.
4. Plan selection by native padded index and draw-key cost, collision support,
   material residency and explicit gameplay behavior requirements.
5. Compile native draw/cell/collision structures, dependency-closed materials,
   catalogue and authored/adapted entities with checked ranges and relocations.
6. Bake surface lighting and native character probes with distinct menu/gameplay
   environments; reserve all chart allocations and use hardware light remaps.
7. Validate structure and native behavior, retain screenshots/logs/trace evidence,
   then package and hash a clean Northstar release with rollback.

Suggested commands `inspect`, `extract`, `plan`, `compile`, `bake`, `validate`
and `package` are proposed interfaces, not existing unified CLI functionality.

## Intermediate representation

Retain every original entity key/value pair and placement ID. Record source and
target origin/angles/scale/skin, selected author LOD, material assignments,
geometry hashes, backend and disposition. Intentional grounding or replacement
deltas need explicit reason and before/after data; never overwrite original origin.

Collision records need owner, source kind (world BVH, inline STAR, IRPS,
embedded BVH, visual fallback or adaptation), target representation, active flag,
contents, geometry hash and disabled reason. Produce one final active ownership
ledger rather than forcing readers to merge historical repair overlays.

Materials need source alias, target GUID, shader provenance, channel mappings,
alpha mode, dependency closure and fidelity adaptations. Visibility needs actual
geometry bounds, camera envelope and mode (`conservative` or validated portals).
Lighting needs caster/receiver masks, native light mapping, atlas reservations,
probes and isolated menu environment. Distinguish capacity limits, field ranges
and project margins in the same budget report.

Stages need implementation hash, input/output hashes, status, diagnostics and
reproducible parameters. Omissions need a source ID, reason and recovery
requirements. Reasons include budget, missing source, unsupported layout,
unsupported behavior, outside selection, deliberate adaptation and unverified.

The existing design contract is
`docs/conversion/conversion-project.schema.json`; historical scripts do not all
serialize that schema yet. Layout headers, 128-slot ledgers and versioned source
manifests provide a starting implementation reference.

## Separate backends and future work

World baking is tested and simplifies static recovery, but consumes world
submission capacity and discards dynamic LOD, animation and instancing. Dense
foliage and repeated props motivate a native-model backend; it needs independent
format, loading, collision and native-render capacity validation. It cannot inherit
the world-path limits or be called complete because one mesh export succeeded.

A true spatial streaming backend needs native coverage/residency semantics and
VRAM-pressure tests. A selective portal backend needs sky-preserving interior
connectivity and camera sweeps. Gameplay adaptation needs objectives, navigation,
conditional entity states and lifecycle validation separately from geometry.
Source identity matches do not certify behavior equivalence.

MRVN-Radiant was evaluated as a development/compiler starting point, not a complete
editor or universal Apex import pipeline. The project pins commit
`8022aefcf9506786fe9edf138dbf48cde0fa82f6` and retains a compiler patch. That is
historical provenance, not a claim about the current state of any upstream fork.

## Sources

`docs/conversion/APEX_TO_TITANFALL2.md`, `conversion-project.schema.json`,
`TOOLCHAIN.md`, `toolchain-versions.json`, `SOURCE_INDEX.md`,
`respawn_conversion_layouts.h`, `docs/composite/CONVERSION.md`, and the latest
map validation receipts. See [case studies](port-case-studies.md) for concrete
scope and remaining omissions.

# R5Reloaded source-map testing and paired Northstar captures

Evidence scope: installed R5R `v2.6.52`, October 12, 2026. These findings come
from the native game, local SDK source, controller tests and captured images.
They do not establish compatibility with every R5R release.

## Controller and installation

The project now has `r5-harness/harness.py`, `protocol.py`, a small Squirrel
helper, JSON routes and `Run-R5Harness.ps1`. It launches the installed executable
directly, loads maps, controls a fixed camera and requests the game's native
`screenshot` command. TGA captures are converted to PNG without changing their
pixels. Metadata records map, origin, angles, requested FOV, dimensions, VM
state, generation, capture time and SHA-256.

The test installation is a separate owned directory. Large immutable asset
directories are hardlinked on the same volume; scripts, configs, executables
and mutable files are independent copies. Staging refuses an unowned directory
and unlinks a destination before replacing it, avoiding writes through an asset
hardlink. The copied base compile list includes the helper. Existing SDK mods
are copied because the installed scripts/playlists depend on their assets.
This isolates installation edits, not the entire Windows user account.

The offline development playlist is `dev_default`. Use `cl_setname MapHarness`
when bypassing the SDK launcher; an empty offline name is rejected during
signon. The engine executes its own RCON configuration after command-line
options, so that copied configuration must retain the harness settings. Wait
for `SIGNONSTATE_FULL` before accessing map script VMs.
Phase Runner first disconnected with `#DISCONNECT_NETCHAN_OVERFLOW` immediately
after full signon under the inherited 120-player development setup. A copied
two-player playlist and `net_processTimeBudget 0` kept the native session alive.
Both settings changed together; this is not an isolated causal test, and the
two-player configuration is a harness setting rather than an engine/map limit.

## Installed console protocol

The installed v2.6.52 envelope differs from the June 2025 upstream SDK schema.
The observed layout is saved as `r5-harness/netcon-v2.6.proto`. Its descriptive
field names are local documentation of the exercised wire contract.

The frame header is two network-order 32-bit integers: magic `0x6e6f4352`, then
protobuf envelope length. The envelope has a nested header in field 1, nonce
bytes in field 2, authentication-tag bytes in field 3 and message bytes in field
4. The nested header has sequence in field 1 and a 64-bit nonce in field 2.
Requests and responses retain the older messageId/messageType/type/message/value
fields 1–5. Sequence starts at one independently in each direction per socket.

Control binds to IPv6 loopback on a separate host port. Frames are unencrypted
only within that local harness; authentication uses a random runtime password.
Passwords and console keys are excluded from exported logs and documentation.
The controller preserves partial frames across socket polling timeouts and
checks incoming sequence order.

Script prints are not consistently echoed over RCON in this installed SDK.
Native `platform/logs/<session>/script.log` is an additional acknowledgement
channel. Every command carries a random ticket. An old log entry cannot satisfy
a new ticket. Server/client VM instance IDs distinguish a completed reload from
stale same-map state. Process stopping checks both liveness and creation time;
a missing creation timestamp cannot authorize termination.

## Camera and comparison semantics

Route coordinates are Titanfall camera/eye positions. For the original Apex
Phase Runner, add `[26000,19000,0]`; Drop-Off uses zero offset. Angles are
`[pitch,yaw,roll]` in degrees. Both engines receive the same angles and FOV and
must produce the same capture resolution. R5R also moves the server player near
the camera and uses noclip, keeping gravity and streaming from pulling its
viewpoint away. Native camera origin/angles can be recorded independently of
the requested values.

First-run agreements require the user's decision. Gameplay message panels are
cleared after that decision. Titanfall's opening countdown can still overlay a
valid camera view; wait for it before taking comparison captures.

Comparison runs are sequential by default to avoid keeping both games in
memory. Source captures are saved before closing the owned R5R process.
`--resume` reuses those source images after checking their route and SHA-256.
The target side uses an already healthy matching map or a fresh owned launch.
Do not force an unnecessary same-map reload after `Northstar.start` has already
loaded the target. During this test, that redundant reload returned to the main
menu; a fresh launch completed the paired route.

The gallery contains side-by-side views, an opacity overlay and capture
metadata. It is evidence for geometry, placement and visual completeness.
Different shaders, lighting, banners, HUDs and tonemapping prevent a pixel-exact
assertion of port correctness. These camera captures do not certify collision,
AI navigation, framerate, networking or game-mode behavior.

Related: [Native Northstar testing](testing-and-packaging.md),
[Case studies](port-case-studies.md), [Visibility and limits](visibility-and-limits.md).
